items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Charlie Parker and Dizzy Gillespie would be awarded an Esquire Magazine award by Leonard Feather.

ctx.x: Did you notice a difference in playing over there? Because a number of people have talked about the difference in the way the music is accepted, or the artists, between the United States and Europe.

Well at that time it was quite noticeable. I’m not sure you could say — I think you could say it’s the same now. Europeans came to appreciate jazz as an art form earlier than, ironically, earlier than we did in America. They got into it in a scholarly way, and a critical way, earlier than anybody else did, with the exception of people like Leonard Feather perhaps. But even in the 20’s, the French were into jazz and Charles Delaunay was the first person to think of doing a discography of jazz recordings. That was…
It seems like sometimes the — something that comes from somewhere else has an exotic quality to it.
